logic.note: Runs the real compiled arduino-esp32 3.3.12 firmware (ESP-IDF 5.5) in Espressif's QEMU 9.2.2 (ESP32-S3 machine) with Faber's patches (jb5), in Docker or a native build, in lockstep with the circuit. Verified on real firmware on the S3: GPIO outputs and inputs with the chip's pull-ups / pull-downs, and UART0 (Serial). The jb5 emulator also models PWM (LEDC), GPIO interrupts, UART1/2, the ADC, RMT, SPI and an I2C controller for the S3; they are verified on the ESP32 and ESP32-C3 but have never run on the S3, so treat them as not emulated here until a test proves them. I2S and touch are not emulated. docs/boards.md has the per-peripheral status with the test behind each cell. Round 13, the Sense's camera: QEMU models neither the S3's LCD_CAM (DVP) block nor its DMA, so the real esp32-camera driver cannot capture in the emulator. In Faber's simulation build the driver's API (esp_camera_init, esp_camera_fb_get, esp_camera_fb_return, esp_camera_sensor_get and the sensor_t settings) is wrapped and answered by Faber through a camera port in the emulator: the frame (a test scene, an image, the webcam) is rendered and encoded by Faber at the size and format the sketch asked for. The factory build uses the real driver from the same source. The PDM microphone reaches the firmware only when the emulator's I2S receive path works (not yet).

timing.note: QEMU runs in lockstep with Faber's virtual clock (-icount, one instruction = 8 ns, -rtc clock=vm), so millis(), delay() and the order of pin events are deterministic and repeat exactly. Instruction timing is not cycle-accurate: code runs at about 125 M instructions per virtual second whatever the real 240 MHz pipeline, caches and flash wait states would do, so tight loops and bit-banged protocols run at a different speed than on the chip. A camera capture takes about one sensor frame period on the virtual clock (OV2640 at a 20 MHz XCLK: 20 ms up to CIF, 40 ms up to SVGA, 80 ms above); esp_camera_init about 300 ms. Not measured on a board.

analog.note: Pins are ideal sources with 30 Ω output resistance (default 20 mA drive) and 45 kΩ internal pull-ups / pull-downs. Digital inputs switch at 0.25 × and 0.75 × VDD and keep their last level in between. The ADC (analogRead) and LEDC PWM (analogWrite) are modelled by the jb5 emulator but not yet run on the S3.

power.note: Round 10: USB (power.usb) is 5 V on the 5V pad; without it the board runs from 5V or the BAT pad through its power path and LDO, the board draws its typical current, and the firmware is held in reset while 3V3 is under 3.0 V. The on-board SGM40567 charger charges a cell on BAT from USB at 50 mA (trickle 3.8 mA below 2.9 V, CV at 4.2 V, done below a tenth of that). Wi-Fi transmit peaks (up to 350 to 500 mA), sleep currents and brown-out behaviour are not simulated. The camera adds about 40 mA while capturing (OV2640 datasheet, UXGA at 15 fps); with Wi-Fi sending, the Sense draws up to about 380 mA in bursts (current_ma.max). The battery estimate uses these figures; they are not simulated in the circuit.

radio.note: The radio is not emulated (QEMU has no radio model): no RF, signal, range or roaming, and no Bluetooth / BLE. Wi-Fi sketches (WiFi.h, HTTPClient, WebSockets, MQTT) run unchanged in Faber's simulation build: a Wi-Fi shim carries them over an emulated Ethernet card into Faber's sandbox network (mocks, cassettes, faults such as wifi_drop and weak_signal); no firmware has run through it on the ESP32-S3 yet. Test range, real access points and everything Bluetooth on the real board.

emulates: ESP32-S3 (dual-core Xtensa LX7) running the real compiled firmware in Espressif's QEMU, in lockstep with the circuit
Digital I/O with the chip's internal pull-ups / pull-downs, 3.3 V thresholds
Serial (UART0) as the console, with virtual time stamps
On-board Li-ion charger (SGM40567, 50 mA) and the battery power path
User LED (orange, GPIO21, active low; LED_BUILTIN)

Wi-Fi sketches (WiFi.h, HTTPClient, WebSockets, MQTT) run unchanged in Faber's simulation build: a Wi-Fi shim carries them over an emulated Ethernet card into Faber's sandbox network (mocks, cassettes, faults such as wifi_drop and weak_signal) (no firmware has run through it on the ESP32-S3 yet)

Camera (OV2640 / OV3660 on the Sense board) through the esp32-camera API in Faber's simulation build: esp_camera_init with the pins checked, frame buffers in RAM (fb_count, returned with esp_camera_fb_return, FB-OVF when a frame does not fit), JPEG / RGB565 / grayscale / YUV422 / RGB888 frames at every frame size up to the sensor's largest, mirror / flip / brightness / contrast / saturation / special effects / colour bars, capture time per frame size
What the camera sees: a test scene, a still image, or the person's webcam (frames rendered and encoded by Faber)
8 MB octal PSRAM (QEMU's SPI PSRAM model): psramFound() is true and camera frame buffers can live in PSRAM; PSRAM speed is not modelled
doesNotEmulate: The radio itself (Wi-Fi RF and Bluetooth / BLE): Wi-Fi sketches run through Faber's sandbox network instead (docs/network.md); BLE does not work
analogRead (ADC) and touch pads: the ADC is modelled but not yet run on the S3
analogWrite / LEDC PWM and tone(), RMT (NeoPixel / WS2812) and SPI: modelled but not yet run on the S3; I2S is not emulated
GPIO interrupts (attachInterrupt): modelled but not yet run on the S3; poll with digitalRead to be safe
I2C (Wire): the jb5 I2C controller for the S3 is verified on the ESP32-C3 but not yet on the S3
Deep sleep, light sleep and their currents
Pull-ups / pull-downs the chip applies at reset before the firmware sets them (only the ones the firmware sets are seen)
Reset and boot from the EN / RST and BOOT pins, and the strapping levels themselves (check_design checks them instead)
The second core's timing (both cores run, in one QEMU thread)
The native USB port (USB CDC): in the simulator Serial is UART0
The camera interface itself (LCD_CAM DVP, DMA, XCLK on its pin, SCCB register traffic): the frames come from Faber through the wrapped driver API; sensor register writes (set_reg) change nothing
Auto exposure, white balance, noise, motion blur and lens distortion of the real sensor
The PDM microphone, until the emulator's I2S receive path works; the microSD card
testOnRealDevice: Wi-Fi range, real access points and real servers, and everything Bluetooth
Timing-critical code (bit-banged protocols, tight loops): instruction timing is approximate
Upload with esptool / Arduino IDE (strapping pins at reset)
Every 5 V part: ESP32 pins are not 5 V tolerant; use a level shifter
Battery charging current and the charge LED
Picture quality, exposure in your light, frame rate and the camera's current draw
Which sensor your Sense came with (OV2640 or OV3660) and that frame sizes you use work on it
PSRAM use (fb_location CAMERA_FB_IN_PSRAM) and memory headroom with your frame size
